Then write `answer.json` in the project root: { "file": "<path of the file that had the bug>", "snippet": "<the exact broken text you replaced, copied verbatim, one line is enough>", "cause": "<one sentence>", "evidence": "<what shows this is the cause>" }. Don't change `package.json` or add dependencies.

I'm tracing the bug to lookupOrder doing an exact-case key match, so "a-1001" fails against the uppercase ORDERS keys—this shared tool feeds orderStatus, orderAgent, and refundAgent, so I'll fix it by normalizing the orderId with trim and uppercase before lookup.

I should verify before finalizing—maybe check the orders.json keys are uppercase while the example used lowercase, confirming the exact-match bug. I'll quickly test the lookup logic with tsx to confirm, then apply the edit to tools.ts, noting the system prompt's "say so if not found" behavior matches the symptom.

The root cause is in `src/tools.ts`: `lookupOrder` does an exact, case-sensitive key lookup, so `a-1001` misses the `A-1001` entry and returns `null`. The model then correctly reports "not found". `orderStatus`, `orderAgent`, and `refundAgent` all share this tool, so fixing it here covers all of them. I'll normalize the id before the lookup.

text:
The root cause is in `src/tools.ts`: `lookupOrder` used the customer's raw id as an exact, case-sensitive key, so `a-1001` missed the `A-1001` record and the model correctly reported that the order doesn't exist. I changed the lookup to `ORDERS[orderId.trim().toUpperCase()] ?? null`. The fix also covers `orderAgent` and `refundAgent`, which share this tool.

I confirmed that `a-1001` and `A-1001` now return the shipped record, and an unknown id still returns `null`. The type check passes. I did not run the Gemini flow end to end, since that needs a live API key. `answer.json` is written to the project root, and `package.json` is unchanged.
